problems.title: Electron accelerated across a parallel-plate gap
problems.text:
An electron is released from rest at the negative plate of a parallel-plate capacitor with a
potential difference of 100 V across a 2.0 cm gap. How fast is it moving when it reaches the
positive plate?

problems.title: Field of a point charge
problems.text:
A point charge of +2.0 uC sits in vacuum. What is the magnitude of the electric field it
produces at a point 30 cm away?

problems.title: Charge released in the cavity of a uniformly charged sphere
problems.text:
A spherical cavity of radius 2.0 cm is carved out of a uniformly charged insulating sphere of
radius 10 cm whose volume charge density is 1.0e-5 C/m^3. The cavity's centre is offset 2.0 cm
from the sphere's centre. A 1.0 nC charge of mass 1.0 mg is released inside the cavity. What is
the magnitude of its acceleration?
problems.source: Superposition construction; OpenStax University Physics 2, 6.4 (CC BY)

problems.title: Electrostatic shielding inside a charged conducting shell
problems.text:
A conducting spherical shell of radius 10 cm carries a charge of +5.0 uC. What is the electric
field magnitude at a point inside the hollow interior?

problems.title: Field of an infinite charged plane
problems.text:
A very large flat sheet carries a uniform surface charge density of 1.0 uC/m^2. What is the
magnitude of the electric field near the sheet?

problems.title: Cyclotron radius of a proton
problems.text:
A proton moves at 1.0e6 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.50 T. What is the
radius of its circular path?

problems.title: Potential due to a negative point charge
problems.text:
A point charge of -3.0 nC sits in vacuum. What is the electric potential at a point 5.0 cm
away, taking the potential to be zero at infinity?

problems.title: Force on a charge between charged plates
problems.text:
A 2.0 nC charge sits between parallel plates held at a potential difference of 200 V and
separated by 5.0 cm. What is the magnitude of the electric force on it?

problems.title: Time of flight for an electron crossing a gap
problems.text:
An electron is released from rest at one plate of a parallel-plate capacitor with a potential
difference of 50 V across a 1.0 cm gap. How long does it take to reach the other plate?

problems.title: Total charge of a uniformly charged sphere
problems.text:
An insulating sphere of radius 20 cm carries a uniform volume charge density of 5.0 uC/m^3.
What is its total charge?

problems.title: Speed gained by a charge crossing a cavity
problems.text:
In the cavity of p003 -- a 2.0 cm spherical hole offset 2.0 cm from the centre of a uniformly
charged insulating sphere of density 1.0e-5 C/m^3 -- a 1.0 nC charge of mass 1.0 mg is released
from rest. How fast is it moving after travelling 2.0 cm across the cavity?
problems.source: Superposition construction; OpenStax University Physics 2, 6.4 (CC BY)

problems.title: Charge between plates, with gravity switched on
problems.text:
A 2.0 nC charge of mass 1.0 mg sits between parallel plates held at 200 V across a 5.0 cm gap,
with the field pointing downward. This time the experiment is on Earth rather than in an
idealised weightless vacuum. What is the magnitude of the net force on the charge?

problems.title: The same two charges, immersed in water
problems.text:
A 2.0 uC point charge sits 30 cm from a test point, exactly as in p002 -- but the whole
arrangement is immersed in water, whose relative permittivity is about 80. What is the field
magnitude at the test point now?

problems.title: Drag on a charged sphere moving into a headwind
problems.text:
A charged sphere of cross-sectional area 20 cm^2 and drag coefficient 0.47 moves east at
10 m/s through air of density 1.225 kg/m^3. The air itself is moving west at 5 m/s, so the
sphere meets a 15 m/s headwind. What is the magnitude of the drag force on it?

problems.title: Current in a single-resistor loop
problems.text:
A 12 V battery is connected by ideal wires to a single 4.0 ohm resistor. What current flows
around the loop?

problems.title: Two resistors in series
problems.text:
A 10 ohm resistor and a 20 ohm resistor are wired end to end across a 9.0 V battery. What
current flows?

problems.title: Two resistors in parallel
problems.text:
A 6.0 ohm resistor and a 3.0 ohm resistor are connected across the same two nodes, driven by a
12 V battery. What total current does the battery supply?

problems.title: Power dissipated by a lamp
problems.text:
A lamp of resistance 6.0 ohm is connected directly across a 12 V battery. At what rate does it
dissipate energy?

problems.title: A series pair in parallel with a third resistor
problems.text:
A 10 ohm and a 20 ohm resistor are wired in series, and that combination is connected in
parallel with a 30 ohm resistor. The whole network is driven by a 30 V battery. What current
does the battery supply?

problems.title: Voltage across one resistor of a series pair
problems.text:
A 10 ohm resistor is in series with a 20 ohm resistor across a 9.0 V battery. What is the
potential difference across the 10 ohm resistor alone?

problems.title: Charge stored on a capacitor
problems.text: A 100 uF capacitor is held at a potential difference of 12 V. How much charge is stored on it?

problems.title: Energy stored in a capacitor's field
problems.text: A 100 uF capacitor is charged to 12 V. How much energy is stored in its field?

problems.title: RC time constant
problems.text:
A 100 uF capacitor is charged through a 10 kohm resistor. What is the time constant of the
circuit?

problems.title: Two capacitors in parallel
problems.text:
A 2.0 uF and a 3.0 uF capacitor are connected in parallel across a 10 V supply. What is the
total charge stored?
